newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cattle breeders stage mad cow protests.
newsitem.headline: French cattle breeders stage mad cow protests.

text.p: Cattle breeders blocked roads, airports and rail links in central France on Friday demanding government aid to make up for falling meat consumption over fears of mad cow disease, police and unions said.
Hundreds of farmers joined protests in about 20 of France's 96 departments, they said. The actions were concentrated in the Limousin, Auvergne and Burgundy regions.
Groups of farmers blocked runways at the Limoges and Lepaud airports and cut off rail traffic on the Paris-Clermont Ferrand and Paris-Toulouse lines.
A key marshalling yard was also shut down in the central town of La Souterraine.
Trains were being diverted to Toulouse by way of Bordeaux and to Limoges via Poitiers, the state rail authority SNCF said.
Farmers were also blocking numerous local roads as well as several major highways including the A20 autoroute between Paris and Toulouse.
Other groups of farmers were dumping loads of cow manure in front of tax offices.

Farmers unions leaders say farm income has plummeted as meat sales have dropped by up to 25 percent due to fears that mad cow disease, known scientifically as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), might be able to infect humans.
The unions want government subsidies of 1,000 francs ($200) per dairy cow to help them through the crisis.
British scientists said this week they had found more evidence that mad cow disease, most prevalent in Britain, could spread to people.
Their research published on Wednesday found a new variant of fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans left traces very similar to the brain-wasting mad cow disease.
